questions.question: What is the most common type of crash for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania?

options.text: Single vehicle crash or running off the road.
Being hit on the side on an interstate.
Driving in reverse on a side street.
Driving on the shoulder of a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single vehicle crash or running off the road.
questions.explanation: The most common crash for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania is a single-vehicle crash where the car leaves the road. From 2009 to 2011, there were 2,293 of these crashes and 45 deaths.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic from both directions cannot cross the center line to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces concentration. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when emotionally upset.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Give the motorcycle only half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same rights as other vehicles. Give motorcyclists a full lane width so they can maneuver safely.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: The "Four-second rule" tells you how to:

options.text: Yield to other cars.
Turn at stop signs.
Stay a safe distance behind another car.
Cross an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay a safe distance behind another car.
questions.explanation: On dry pavement, leave at least four seconds of distance between your vehicle and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and mark the road's right edge. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: On a dry highway, a safe following distance is at least:

options.text: Three seconds.
Two seconds.
Four seconds.
Two car lengths.

questions.explanation: On a dry highway, keep at least four seconds between you and the car ahead. This gives you enough time to steer or brake if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and be careful.
Drive through normally.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when it is safe.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be careful. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Stay right on hills.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from the road surface. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane, or slide on the water.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake suddenly to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If someone follows too closely, slow down gradually to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What is a blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in any mirror. They are usually to the sides and behind your car.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you enter the exit lane.
When you see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well before your exit. Only slow down after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. What matters is not the type of drink, but the total amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.
